paraphrase: One who is impure (through birth- or death-impurity) is not eligible for divine or ancestral rites — except the Kula worship of the Primordial One and rites already begun; those over five years old are cremated in the cremation ground; a Kula woman is not to be burnt with her husband: woman is your own form, Goddess, her body veiled in the world, and if out of delusion she mounts her husband's pyre she goes to hell.

paraphrase: The symbolism of Kālī's form: as white, yellow and other colours disappear in black, so all beings enter Kālī — hence the formless power of Time is described as black; the moon on her forehead signifies her immortality; her three eyes are moon, sun and fire, by which she sees the whole world born of time; her boon- and fear-dispelling hands protect beings in danger and impel them to their tasks; she is seated on a red lotus because she stands on the worlds born of rajas; pure consciousness, witness of all, she watches Time playing drunk on the wine of delusion; thus forms are imagined according to her qualities for the good of devotees of little understanding.
